UNDERSTANDING FRACTIONS
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what understanding fractions means in plain words.
• Give one Kenyan example linked to Fractions.
• Correct one common mistake about this page.

INTRODUCTION
----
Get clear on fractions before moving on. On “Understanding Fractions”, how would you explain fractions to a classmate in one minute? Use this anchor: Identify the numerator and denominator in a fraction in different situations,. Clue from the topic: Convert improper fractions to. Check every example on this page against that anchor.

MAIN NOTES
----
• A fraction names equal parts of a whole: numerator (top) counts parts taken; denominator (bottom) counts equal parts in the whole.
• Example: 7/13 means 7 equal parts out of 13.
• Equivalent fractions name the same amount (2/4 = 1/2).
• Always use equal parts — unequal slices are not a fair fraction model.
• In Kenya you meet fractions when sharing chapati, measuring half a litre, or reading a recipe.

WORKED EXAMPLE
----
Worked example on Fractions:
Compare or use the fraction 1/4 in a sharing problem.

Working:
1. Formula / relationship: Fraction = parts taken / equal parts in the whole
2. Substitute values: Fraction = 1/4
3. There are 4 equal parts; 1 part(s) are taken.
4. As a decimal (if needed): 0.25
Final Answer: 1/4
